class: A code-entry page was recognised only by a box named 'code', so a code typed one character per box read as a link to click
symptom: Walmart (careers.walmart.com): after the posting page the site asked for a six-digit code emailed to the owner ('Check your email for the verification code', six boxes 'Digit 1 of 6' ... 'Digit 6 of 6'). The run handed over to the owner with 'the site sent a verification email: open it, click its link, then press Continue'.
root_cause: account_state.read_state treats a page as a code step only when a textbox's own name contains 'code', 'passcode' or 'otp'. Segmented entries name their boxes by position, so the page fell through to the wording rule 'check your email / verification' and was read as VERIFY_EMAIL, which asks the owner to click a link. The step that types a code per box (PageAgent.complete_account_code, built for R+L Carriers) already handled the boxes; only the classifier ahead of it did not see them.
why_tests_missed: The code-step fixtures all had a box whose name carried the word code (or R+L Carriers' 'Enter verification code digit 1 of six'); none named the boxes by position alone.
fix: account_state treats four or more textboxes named like 'Digit 1 of 6' (digit / character / number / box / field, n of m) as a code box, so a page that says 'verification code' beside them is CODE_ENTRY and the next step is ENTER_CODE. Fewer than four such boxes, and a link page with no boxes, read as before.
prevention: Recognise a code entry by what the page asks for (its wording plus any run of input boxes that spell a code), not by one box's name; test a code step with the boxes named by position, by label text outside the box, and as a single box.
